problems.source_says: The paper identifies two external raters, without stating their qualifications or whether they were lay raters or crowd workers. Codebook section 6 defines human_raters as lay raters or crowd workers, distinguishing them from expert_raters. Human assessment is established, but this specific rater subtype is not; its code should remain null unless further source evidence establishes it. This is an unsupported classification, not evidence that the raters were experts.
problems.quote: two external raters independently evaluated employees’ responses to a question on privacy protection in the digital workplace.
problems.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5), Participants and Procedure and Dependent Variable: Creativity; complete saved document checked for rater qualifications. creativity-codebook.md, section 6, Measure.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 correctly records scored_on_output=false: direct supervisors rated general creative performance over the week, rather than an identified product. The overall_creativity construct and professional-supervisor expert_raters classification are supported.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5), Dependent Variable: Creativity; codebook sections 3 and 6.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 concerns the intervention week, during which treated employees had and used personal ChatGPT accounts; ai_available_when_produced=yes and the contextual with_ai classification are supported.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 5-6 (printed pp. 4-5), Participants and Procedure, Experimental Conditions and Manipulation Checks, and Dependent Variable: Creativity.

confirmed.statement: S1-O2 and S1-O3 satisfy criterion 3: two external raters independently assessed novelty and usefulness of employees’ written privacy-protection responses, using 1-5 scales. These are output ratings, not self-reported creativity; ICCs are .78 and .69, respectively.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5), Dependent Variable: Creativity.

confirmed.statement: The novelty and usefulness constructs concern each individual response. They measure neither diversity across different people nor flexibility within one person.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5), Dependent Variable: Creativity; codebook section 6, Construct.

confirmed.statement: All three outcome analyses use participants as the observation unit: 250 employees nested within 30 supervisors and three departments. The two external ratings are not analyzed as 500 independent observations.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5), Results; PDF p. 10 (printed p. 9), Table 3 and its N=250 note.

confirmed.statement: For S1-O2 and S1-O3, the saved paper does not specify whether ChatGPT was available while composing the second-survey response. The form appropriately leaves AI availability and question null; neither with_ai nor after_ai is established for this task.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5), Participants and Procedure and Dependent Variable: Creativity; full saved Methods and Results, PDF pp. 5-10; codebook section 1.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 reported values match: control M=3.05, SD=1.09; LLM M=4.14, SD=0.58; t-test p=.000 as printed; d=1.25; controlled Model 2 gamma=0.84, SE=0.10, p<.001.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 7), Table 2; PDF p. 10 (printed p. 9), Table 3 Model 2; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5), Results.

confirmed.statement: S1-O2 reported values match: control M=2.78, SD=0.96; LLM M=3.11, SD=0.95; t-test p=.006; d=0.35; controlled Model 3 gamma=0.25, SE=0.13, p=.049.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 7), Table 2; PDF p. 10 (printed p. 9), Table 3 Model 3; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5), Results.

confirmed.statement: S1-O3 reported values match: control M=2.87, SD=0.82; LLM M=3.15, SD=0.89; t-test p=.010; d=0.33; controlled Model 4 gamma=0.17, SE=0.11, p=.136. The main Results explicitly report the no-controls estimate as gamma=0.28, SE=0.11, p=.009.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 7), Table 2; PDF p. 10 (printed p. 9), Table 3 Model 4; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5), Results. The no-controls numbers were checked against the main text, not the unavailable supplemental table.

confirmed.statement: The mediator-adjusted LLM coefficients in measure_detail match Table 3: Model 5=0.71 (SE=0.11), Model 6=0.13 (SE=0.13), and Model 7=0.02 (SE=0.12). The 0.17 (SE=0.08, p=.021) novelty coefficient belongs to cognitive job resources.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 9), Table 3, Models 5-7; PDF p. 7 (printed p. 6), H3 results.

confirmed.statement: No additional qualifying output outcome was found in the saved document. The other measures concern mechanisms or controls, and the mediation and moderation analyses reuse the same three creativity measures.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 6-7 (printed pp. 5-6), Measures, Results, and Exploratory Analyses and Robustness Tests; PDF p. 10 (printed p. 9), Table 3.

confirmed.statement: The saved paper reports no across-person diversity outcome or assessment after documented AI removal. Possible long-term overreliance and impaired independent thinking are proposed for future research, not reported findings.
confirmed.locator: Complete saved document, markdown lines 1-536; especially PDF pp. 11-12 (printed pp. 10-11), Limitations and Future Directions.

confirmed.statement: The entire 536-line markdown conversion was read, including references; the 14-page saved PDF contains no appended supplement. Completeness beyond this document remains unverified: access to the supplemental DOI and the named SSRN fallback failed with a socket-permission error.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1), supplemental-materials link, and PDF p. 14 (printed p. 13), end of references; https://doi.org/10.1037/apl0001296.supp and https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5864662, attempted during this check.

summary: The two human_raters codes lack evidence that the external raters were lay raters or crowd workers, as the codebook requires. Eligibility holds because employees’ written responses were independently scored for novelty and usefulness.
